llm.findings:
[AST4] expected: The subprocess call is real, but it is limited to an optional CLI path for invoking the documented canonical gate and does not use a shell; this is a trust-boundary caution, not evidence of hidden or malicious execution.
[TT2] expected: LYGO_STACK_ROOT can influence which external gate script is run, so users must keep that environment variable pointed at a trusted stack; the behavior is disclosed and user-run rather than automatic.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not have a separate explicit permissions manifest in the inspected artifacts, but the security documentation describes file-read, environment, subprocess, and no-network expectations clearly enough for this package to remain coherent.
[SDI-2] expected: Delegation to an external canonical gate broadens the trust boundary, but the skill repeatedly identifies itself as a lightweight pre-filter paired with lygo-protocol-stack-operator and documents the bridge.
llm.guidance: Install only if you want a local text/content validation wrapper. Treat LYGO_STACK_ROOT as sensitive configuration: leave it unset for bundled local checks, or set it only to a trusted LYGO stack you intentionally installed and reviewed.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local text-safety gate with an optional user-run bridge to a separate LYGO stack, and I found no hidden network use, persistence, data harvesting, or destructive behavior.
